- Overestimate prices in bullish sentiment periods; reduce forecast peaks when sentiment is positive but recent highs are followed by negative sentiment.
- Underestimate prices during strong negative sentiment; adjust downward only if sentiment remains negative for 3+ days.
- Avoid overreacting to short-term spikes; if forecast rises sharply after a dip, reduce the magnitude of the spike by 10–15%.
- Mean-revert forecasts toward recent 7-day average if sentiment is neutral or mildly negative.
- If sentiment is consistently positive over 5+ days, slightly increase forecast baseline but cap upward movement at 5% above prior 10-day high.
- Lag correction: if true outcome is lower than forecast by >5% for 3 consecutive days, reduce next forecast by 2–3% to avoid further overestimation.
- For 30-day horizon, avoid forecasting >10% above 14-day moving average unless sentiment is strongly bullish and confirmed over 3 days.
